text:
Semyon Varlamov did nearly everything a goalie can do on Long Island on Friday. It still wasn't close. Winnipeg piled up 5.52 expected goals (the quality of its chances, added up) to the Islanders' 1.98, and Kyle Connor turned enough of them into goals for a 3-1 win, the Jets' third straight.

Connor opened it with a wraparound at 17:04 of the first, assisted by Josh Morrissey and Dylan Samberg. Gabriel Vilardi made it 2-0 on a backhand 76 seconds into the second, and Connor added a power-play wrister at 15:36 for his second goal and third point. He put nine shots on goal. The Jets owned the second, 2.03 to 0.60 in expected goals, and the third was even more lopsided. Varlamov stopped 34 of 37 and saved about 1.9 goals more than those shots deserved, including a 40% look for Morgan Barron in the third. NHL.com's Stefen Rosner put it plainly: "Varlamov has been so good tonight. Given them every chance to come back in this one."

The Islanders never took it. Logan Stanley's snap shot at 5:07 of the third, a 4% chance, was their only goal. Rosner also noted that Pete DeBoer reshuffled lines and shortened his bench as the night went on, and that Matthew Schaefer "has been human these last five or so games." On our replays of every shot, the Islanders won this game 11% of the time.

For Winnipeg, the timing matters. Stuart Skinner made 26 saves on 27 shots, about one goal better than expected, and the Jets now head to New Jersey, where Connor Hellebuyck is set to start against his former team for the first time since the trade, according to Daily Faceoff. Whatever you think of that deal, a night like this one, with the skaters controlling play from start to finish, is the best argument Winnipeg can make that it can win without him. The Jets beat the Islanders in overtime eight days ago too; this time there was no need for extra hockey.
headline: Connor buries the Islanders as Varlamov holds the dam
